description: Insert a mandatory Scope Lock immediately after Request Envelope construction and before mutation routing so assistant-authored plans cannot silently broaden the user-authorized objective.
planning_goal: Make Scope Lock a mandatory first-class gate in every canonical toolchain request, immediately after Request Envelope construction and before Mutation Carrier Router or any repository execution.

scope_lock.original_user_instruction: Can you please make the scope lock? Make it part of the toolchain runtime flow every time, inserted in the proper place. Probably at the very start.
authorized_deliverables: Integrate Scope Lock into the canonical toolchain runtime flow at the start of every request.
Register and exercise Scope Lock in the onboarding/toolchain self-test flow.
forbidden_expansions: Do not modify runtime Lancer behavior.
Do not create or modify GitHub workflows.
Do not add unrelated developer tooling.
Do not generalize beyond enforcing user-authorized scope on canonical requests.

acceptance_criteria: Every canonical request must contain a valid scope_lock with the exact original user instruction, authorized deliverables, authorized paths, and forbidden expansions.
Scope Lock executes immediately after Request Envelope construction and before Mutation Carrier Router evaluation.
A request missing scope_lock fails closed as SCOPE_VIOLATION before mutation routing.
Any declared operation, authoring, move, decomposition, or policy path outside scope_lock.authorized_paths fails closed as SCOPE_VIOLATION.
Capability construction is forbidden by default and requires explicit authorization in the scope lock.
Scope Lock produces a deterministic fingerprint and a machine-readable decision record carried into orchestrator state.
Request Envelope includes the scope-lock fingerprint and treats the original user instruction as root authority rather than allowing planning_goal or acceptance criteria to replace it.
Toolchain Orchestrator self-tests prove missing-lock rejection, path-expansion rejection, and valid-lock acceptance.

Toolchain onboarding runs Scope Lock immediately after Request Envelope and before Mutation Carrier Router and states that the user objective is immutable, obstacles may change means but not goals, and only explicit user authorization may expand scope.
package.json exposes scope-lock and scope-lock:self-test commands.
No runtime Lancer source or GitHub workflow is changed.
non_goals: Redesign the rest of the toolchain.
raw_operations_reason: This is a developer-tool bootstrap/integration change across dev_scripts and package registration. Patch Corridor certifies runtime architectural ownership and previously demonstrated that developer-tool semantics are not a corridor-owned runtime family; raw operations are the documented exception while Toolchain Compatibility Staging and all canonical validation remain authoritative.
